methodologyNotes: 12 notable wake-up lights / sunrise alarm clocks selected as the 2026 buyer comparison set, spanning budget Amazon-native clones, mid-range dedicated sunrise-alarm brands (Lumie, Beurer), subscription-based smart sleep devices (Hatch), a design-led premium lamp (Loftie), a light-only bedside device (Casper Glow), and a smart-home-ecosystem entry (Philips Hue Twilight). All 10 seeds from the brief were verified against manufacturer pages, official spec-sheet PDFs, or first-party retail listings; two corrections and two expansions were made. CORRECTION 1: 'Lumie Bodyclock Luxe 750DAB' does not exist as a US-market SKU — DAB digital radio is a UK/EU-only broadcast standard. Lumie's US storefront (lumie.com/en-us) sells the identical chassis, LEDs, dimensions and sound library as the 'Bodyclock Luxe 700FM', substituting FM radio for DAB; this US-equivalent SKU was used instead, with the substitution noted in its own provenance. CORRECTION 2: Philips Wake-up Light HF3531/60 is marked 'Discontinued' on usa.philips.com as of this research date (Philips' only current actively-sold US wake-up light is the HF3520/60); HF3531 was kept per the brief's explicit seed as a widely-resold, still-relevant step-up reference (7 sounds vs. HF3520's 5), with its discontinued status and last-known $169.99 US MSRP disclosed. Two other Philips SKUs considered as expansions (entry-level HF3510/60 and app-connected HF3670/60 'SmartSleep Connected') were found discontinued too and were dropped rather than stacked into the set. EXPANSIONS: added Beurer WL75 (a genuinely current, widely-sold German competitor with Bluetooth app control and 256-color sunrise/sunset) and Philips Hue Twilight (a 2024-era smart-home-ecosystem sunrise lamp frequently shortlisted in 2026 'best sunrise alarm clock' roundups alongside Hatch/Lumie) to reach 12 products and broaden the comparison beyond dedicated alarm-clock form factors. Primary sources: manufacturer product pages and official spec-sheet PDFs (usa.philips.com, documents.philips.com, hatch.co, lumie.com/en-us, casper.com, beurer.com, byloftie.com) fetched directly; where a manufacturer page loaded without a visible checkout price (common for Philips Personal Health SKUs, which route to retail partners) or blocked automated fetches with rate-limiting, first-party retailer listings (Amazon.com, Best Buy, Walmart) or reputable review outlets with hands-on lab measurements (Tom's Guide, TechAdvisor, optimizeyourbiology.com — both of which independently spectrometer-tested bedside lux output) were used as corroboration and are cited as 'corroboration'. specKeys chosen for real comparability across all 12 units: max_brightness_lux (peak light output; manufacturer-published where available, independently lab-measured bedside lux noted as such in provenance where the manufacturer does not publish a figure — several brands, incl. Hatch, Loftie, Casper and most Lumie models, do not publish lux at all, which is null, not a guess), color_temperature_range_k (published Kelvin range; null where the brand only describes color qualitatively, e.g. 'warm white, orange, red' without numbers), sunrise_duration_min (the manufacturer-stated DEFAULT/fixed sunrise duration in minutes as a plain number where one exists; where only an adjustable RANGE is published with no stated factory default — Lumie Shine 300/Luxe 700FM, Philips Hue Twilight — the range is given as a string instead of a fabricated single number), sunset_simulation (boolean), alarm_sound_count (plain number where an exact or clearly-headlined count exists; Hatch's own marketed headline counts are used for its two entries — 30+ for Restore 2, 80+ for Restore 3 — since Hatch does not publish one universal 'included' count separately from its Hatch+ subscription library, a distinction noted in each entry's provenance), fm_radio, app_control (phone-app or SleepMapper/Hue-app dependent control of any feature, not just music streaming), brightness_levels (discrete step count where published; null for continuous/twist-dial or unpublished step counts), bluetooth (device has Bluetooth for control and/or audio, for either purpose). priceUsd = US starting MSRP or first-party listed price for the base single-unit configuration as of 2026-08-01; several small-brand/Amazon-native SKUs (JALL, hOmeLabs) fluctuate meaningfully with frequent Amazon promotions, which is disclosed in priceNote rather than smoothed away. accessedAt 2026-08-01 on all entries.

products.name: Philips SmartSleep Wake-Up Light HF3520/60
products.priceNote: usa.philips.com does not display a direct checkout price for this SKU (Philips Personal Health routes US sales through retail partners). $76.29 is the current Amazon.com price as of Aug 2026 against a $108.95 list price; a customer review on the Philips page separately cites paying $150 pre-tax at one point, indicating meaningful price volatility for this SKU. Treat as a representative street price, not a fixed MSRP.
products.provenance: usa.philips.com product page confirms 30-min colored sunrise simulation (deep red to bright yellow), sunset/fall-asleep dimming function, 5 built-in natural sounds plus FM radio, tap snooze, no app/account required. Official HF3520 user manual (documents.philips.com PDF, spec sheet p.27) confirms light output ~1–300 lux at 45cm across 20 brightness levels, light color ~1500–2800K, FM band 87.5–108.0 MHz, unit dimensions ~20x20x15cm / 0.76kg, default sunrise time 30 min (adjustable 20–40 min via alarm-button combo). No SleepMapper or other app support on this model.

products.name: Philips Wake-up Light HF3531/60
products.priceNote: Discontinued on usa.philips.com as of Aug 2026 ('Discontinued' banner on the product page); $169.99 was the last widely-corroborated US MSRP for this step-up SKU before discontinuation. Included per brief as a still-relevant, widely resold reference unit (secondary market / remaining retailer stock); Philips' only current actively-sold US wake-up light is the HF3520/60.
products.provenance: Official Philips HF3531/01 product spec sheet (documents.philips.com PDF, issue date 2026-01-15) confirms: 7 natural wake-up sounds + FM radio, no smartphone/app control, 20 brightness settings, light intensity 300 lux, coloured sunrise simulation (red to orange to yellow), sunrise simulating process adjustable 20–40 minutes, sunset simulation included, product dimensions 19.2 (H) x 19.9 (diameter) x 14.6cm (D), weight 730g, midnight light + tap-snooze + reading lamp functions, 2 alarm times. usa.philips.com marks the HF3531/60 variant 'Discontinued' with no listed price; $169.99 last-MSRP figure corroborated via independent retail search.

products.name: Hatch Restore 2
products.priceNote: $169.99 current price on hatch.co as of Aug 2026 (launched at $199 in July 2023; occasional retailer sales go lower). Includes a 30-day trial of the Hatch+ subscription ($4.99/mo or $49.99/yr thereafter) required to unlock the full sound/content library.
products.provenance: hatch.co confirms a sunrise alarm that gradually brightens over 30 minutes before the set wake time (WiFi + free iOS/Android Hatch app required for setup and full control; the device also has onboard buttons), a sound machine marketed as '30+ sounds', and a fading sunset/sleep routine at night. No FM radio, no Bluetooth speaker. Hatch's own support documentation separately states 13 alarm sounds are available free without a Hatch+ subscription, with additional sounds gated behind the paid tier — the 30+ figure used here reflects Hatch's own headline marketing count for the full library, not the free-tier-only count. Dimensions ~7.24 x 2.43 x 5.31 in per manufacturer listing; no published lux or discrete brightness-step count.

products.name: Hatch Restore 3
products.priceNote: $169.99 on hatch.co and Amazon as of Aug 2026, same launch price as the Restore 2 it replaces. Includes a 30-day Hatch+ trial ($4.99/mo or $49.99/yr thereafter); usable without a subscription per Hatch's own FAQ, with a smaller free sound/alarm selection.
products.provenance: hatch.co (redirects to the current Restore 3 product page) and its official Amazon.com listing both headline '80+ sleep sounds' and a gentle sunrise alarm that mimics sunrise brightening; PRNewswire's Hatch launch release describes Restore 3 as a 'phone-free' redesign with re-engineered audio and true on-device controls, available in Putty, Greige and Cocoa. No FM radio or Bluetooth speaker confirmed. Hatch+ subscription (30 days free, then $4.99/mo or $49.99/yr) unlocks the full content library including 20+ sunrise-specific alarm tracks; the base device functions and plays a reduced free sound set without it. No published lux figure or discrete brightness-step count found on any first-party source.

products.name: Casper Glow Light
products.priceNote: $129 regular/'Comp. Value' price for a single Glow Light on casper.com as of Aug 2026 (site-wide promo pricing shown at $103.20 at time of access). A two-pack is $249 regular / $199.20 promo.
products.provenance: casper.com's official product specifications confirm a 36x warm-white LED array plus 12x amber accent LEDs at a fixed 2700K color temperature (no color-changing sunrise gradient like dedicated wake-up lights), Bluetooth connectivity to the iOS-only Casper app, and a built-in gyroscope for twist-to-dim manual brightness (continuous, not stepped — no discrete level count published). The app lets users 'schedule a gradual sunrise' and explicitly markets this as a way to 'skip the harsh wakeup of alarms' — confirming sunrise/sunset light simulation but with NO built-in speaker, alarm tone, or sound library of any kind (alarm_sound_count = 0). No FM radio. Single unit: height 5.25in, diameter 3.75in, wireless charging base, 5ft cable, IP54 rated. Not marketed by Casper as a full 'alarm clock' — it is a battery/charging-base night light with a sunrise-scheduling feature, included here because it is one of the most frequently compared bedside sunrise-light products in 2026 buying guides.

products.name: Lumie Bodyclock Shine 300
products.priceNote: $169.00 on lumie.com/en-us (official US store) as of Aug 2026, confirmed on both the product page and the wake-up-lights collection page.
products.provenance: lumie.com/en-us official product page confirms: 15–90 minute adjustable sunrise/sunset duration (no single stated default), adjustable sunrise intensity, integrated warm-white/orange/red LED (no Kelvin figures published), 15 sleep/wake sounds, FM radio, tap-control snooze, daily/weekly alarm, light-sensitive auto-dimming display, dimensions 18 (H) x 21 (W) x 12cm (D), weight 0.650kg, 3-year warranty, 45-day trial. No app or Bluetooth. Lumie does not publish a lux spec for this model; optimizeyourbiology.com's independent spectrometer testing (2026 roundup of 15 sunrise clocks) measured the Shine 300 at approximately 360 lux at bedside distance — used here as a lab-measured corroborated figure rather than a manufacturer spec, and should be read as a third-party measurement, not an official rating.

products.name: Lumie Bodyclock Luxe 700FM
products.priceNote: $259.00 on lumie.com/en-us (official US store) as of Aug 2026. NOTE: the brief's seed 'Lumie Bodyclock Luxe 750DAB' is not sold in the US — DAB digital radio is a UK/EU-only broadcast standard. Lumie's US storefront sells the same lamp body, LEDs, dimensions and sound library under the name 'Bodyclock Luxe 700FM', with FM radio substituted for DAB; that US-market SKU is used here as the direct correction of the seed.
products.provenance: lumie.com/en-us official product page confirms: 15–90 minute adjustable sunrise/sunset duration, integrated low-blue white / blue-enriched white / orange / red LEDs (no Kelvin figures published), FM radio, high-quality Bluetooth speaker for streaming, 27 sleep/wake sounds (marketed headline copy rounds this to '25+'), dimensions 20 (H) x 23 (W) x 13cm (D), weight 1.39kg, tap-control snooze, daily/weekly alarm, 3-year warranty, 45-day trial. No app control (physical dial/button controls only). Third-party healf.com listing (a US retailer) corroborates the identical spec sheet and confirms US availability of the 700FM name in place of the UK '750DAB' designation.

products.name: Loftie Lamp
products.priceNote: $280 at byloftie.com (official Loftie store) as of Aug 2026; a certified-refurbished unit is sold at a discount with a 1-year warranty for buyers on a budget.
products.provenance: byloftie.com's official product description confirms the sunrise alarm illuminates from the base and moves up the full column, growing brighter, 'taking 9 minutes from start to finish' — notably shorter and fixed versus competitors' 20–90 minute adjustable ranges. Sunset mode does a slow fade to ease into rest. The lamp has three fixed modes (Day, Reading, Night) plus two customizable modes for color/brightness, RGB + warm-white LEDs, polycarbonate shell with steel top shade, lithium-ion battery, dimensions 16in (H) x 11.5in (W) x 9in (D) with shade, weight 2.12 lbs. Works with the Loftie app/content ecosystem (curated white noise, nature sounds, meditations, sound baths, breathwork, bedtime stories) — no fixed 'alarm sound count' is published since content is a rotating curated library rather than a fixed onboard set. No FM radio; no lux or Kelvin specs published; Bluetooth capability not explicitly confirmed on the product page (left null rather than assumed).

products.name: JALL Wake Up Light Sunrise Alarm Clock
products.priceNote: $34.95 typical Amazon.com list price as of Aug 2026; frequently discounted (spotted as low as ~$31, and a related-listing widget showed $38.24 for a similar JALL SKU) — this is an Amazon-native brand with volatile, promotion-driven pricing rather than a fixed MSRP.
products.provenance: Amazon.com official listing (model covering kids/heavy-sleeper positioning) confirms sunrise light simulation up to light-intensity level 20 (~320 lux), dual alarms, FM radio, snooze, 7 nightlight colors, 7 natural wake-up sounds. This specific SKU's title and description do not mention a fading sunset/dusk feature (unlike JALL's separate 'Full-Screen' product line, which does advertise sunset simulation and a Bluetooth speaker) — sunset_simulation is therefore set to false rather than assumed true for this exact model. No app or Bluetooth on this SKU. No published Kelvin or default sunrise-duration figure (dawn duration is adjustable 0–60 minutes per the on-device menu, with no stated factory default). JALL is an Amazon-marketplace brand without a dedicated corporate website; pricing and specs are sourced directly from the retail listing.

products.name: hOmeLabs Sunrise Alarm Clock
products.priceNote: ~$22.99 typical Amazon.com price as of Aug 2026 for this entry-level SKU; an older Newegg listing for the same model is no longer live, and homelabs.com's own current storefront does not list this product — it appears to be sold as an Amazon-marketplace-only legacy SKU rather than a flagship item on the brand's own site.
products.provenance: Amazon.com official listing and product title confirm: digital LED clock with 6-color switch, FM radio, multiple nature sounds, sunset simulation, touch control, snooze function, 12/24-hour display, warm-white LED that turns on 30 minutes before the set alarm time and gradually brightens until wake-up, 5V DC / 100–240V AC adapter, FM band 88–108 MHz, unit dimensions approx. 3.93 x 6.85 x 7.2in. No lux, Kelvin, exact sound count, app, or Bluetooth specs are published by the manufacturer on any first-party or reputable secondary source found — left null rather than guessed. No verifiable direct manufacturer or press image file could be confirmed (Amazon's listing images are gated behind bot-detection on automated fetch, and homelabs.com's own current catalog does not carry this product), so no image is included per sourcing discipline.

products.name: Beurer WL75 Wake-Up Light
products.priceNote: $89.99 MSRP, corroborated at Best Buy (SKU 6477079) as of Aug 2026; also sold via shop-beurer.com and Amazon.com at the same price point.
products.provenance: Beurer's official US product page confirms: simulated sunlight sunrise/sunset with colored light at 2000 lux intensity (the unit separately claims 3000 lux at ~15cm when used purely as a reading lamp — the 2000 lux sunrise-mode figure is used here as the comparable spec), 6 wake-up melodies and 4 separate fall-asleep melodies (6 used for alarm_sound_count as the wake-facing figure), FM radio, 256 customizable colors via the free Bluetooth 'beurer LightUp' app (or 10 presets without the app), 2 adjustable alarm times, 1–30 minute snooze, product dimensions 8.9 x 7.3 x 3.7in, weight 2 lbs. No published Kelvin range (RGB color system rather than a white-temperature spec) and no stated default sunrise duration in minutes.

products.name: Philips Hue White and Color Ambiance Twilight
products.priceNote: $279.99 US MSRP per Philips Hue / retailer listings as of Aug 2026; UK RRP is £249.99, occasionally discounted by third-party retailers (e.g. to £199.99 at John Lewis in the UK).

specs.color_temperature_range_k: 2000–6500 K (Hue White and Color Ambiance platform range; not confirmed Twilight-specific)

products.provenance: TechAdvisor's hands-on review confirms: dual light sources (an adjustable front lampshade plus a rear gradient LED strip) that ramp brightness and shift from warm to cool to simulate sunrise, sunrise duration configurable to 10/20 or 30 minutes, a 'go-to-sleep' automation that gradually dims for a sunset effect, six preset lighting scenes, Philips Hue app control over Bluetooth (Zigbee/Hue Bridge also supported for full smart-home integration), voice control via Alexa/Google Home/Apple Home/SmartThings, one-press sleep-routine button on top, ~33cm tall, ~990g, matte plastic construction with a cork base, available in black or white. Explicitly has 'no audio option' — no speaker, no alarm tones, no FM radio (alarm_sound_count = 0). TechRadar's independent spectrometer testing measured 395 lux at bedside, used here as a lab-measured figure. The 2000–6500K range reflects Philips Hue's general White and Color Ambiance color-temperature platform spec and is not confirmed as a Twilight-specific published figure, flagged accordingly. Included as an expansion pick: an app/smart-home-ecosystem sunrise light frequently shortlisted alongside Hatch and Lumie in 2026 buying guides, representing a distinct product category (smart bulb/lamp vs. dedicated alarm clock) that buyers actively compare against the others in this set.
